cards.text: Jesus is in the temple courts, and the chief priests and Pharisees already know His parables are about them (Matthew 21:45). Once again, Jesus speaks in parables, and He says the kingdom of heaven is like a king who prepares a wedding banquet. A wedding banquet? Friend, now you're speaking MY language.

cards.question: In Jesus' parable, who is the king throwing this wedding banquet for?

cards.text: The king sends his servants to call the people he invited. This is the part where everybody's supposed to grab their coat.

cards.question: True or false: When the king's servants call the invited guests, the guests come to the banquet.

cards.text: So the king sends other servants with a message: "I have prepared my dinner. My oxen and fattened cattle have been killed, and everything is ready. Come to the wedding banquet."

cards.question: The king says everything is ready. What do some of the invited guests do?

answers.text: Ignore him and go off to work
Ask him to pick a later date

cards.text: One goes off to his field, another to his business. The KING calls, and these guys hit snooze.

cards.question: The rest of the invited guests go even further with the king's servants. What do they do?
The king is enraged. He sends his ___ to destroy those murderers and burn their ___.

cards.text: Then the king tells his servants, "The wedding banquet is ready, but those I invited were not worthy." The guest list fell apart, but friend, the oven doesn't care who RSVP'd, and dinner is still READY.

cards.question: With the banquet ready, the king tells his servants to go to the ___ and invite people.
True or false: The king tells his servants to invite only the most important people they find at the crossroads.

cards.text: So the servants head out into the streets and start gathering guests. Me, with a whole banquet hall to fill? I'd yell FREE COOKIES and get out of the way.

cards.question: Who do the servants gather from the streets for the king's banquet?

cards.text: The wedding hall is filled with guests, wall to wall. Then the king comes in to see them, and he spots one man.

cards.question: What does the king notice about this one man in the wedding hall?

answers.text: He isn't dressed in wedding clothes
He came in without being invited
He's sitting in the king's own seat

cards.question: The king says, "Friend," and asks, "how did you get in here without wedding clothes?" The man is ___.

cards.text: Then the king tells the servants, "Tie him hand and foot, and throw him into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth." Friend, I spent years in the dark of a junk drawer, and that was nothing like this.

cards.question: Jesus ends the parable with a line about who is called and who is chosen. True or false: He says everyone who is called is also chosen.

cards.text: "For many are called, but few are chosen." That's where Jesus ends this parable, friend, but He's not done in the temple, and neither are we.

findings.problem: The opening card has four sentences: 'Jesus is in the temple courts...', 'Once again, Jesus speaks in parables...', 'A wedding banquet?' and 'Friend, now you're speaking MY language.' The limit is three.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: 'Jesus is in the temple courts' comes from outside the passage (Matthew 21:23), but the card gives no reference for it. Only the Matthew 21:45 fact has one.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The joke mixes Papa Dorin's oven with the king's banquet. 'The oven doesn't care who RSVP'd, and dinner is still READY' runs his comparison and the Bible setting together in one image. It also repeats the 'ready' the quote just said.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: 'So the servants head out...', 'Me, with a whole banquet hall to fill?' and 'I'd yell FREE COOKIES and get out of the way.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
